name: Neon
description: Self-hosted Neon — serverless Postgres with database branching, a web console and per-branch connection strings, in a single container. Built on the community `neond` control plane (Apache-2.0), which bundles Neon's pageserver, safekeeper, storage broker and storage controller behind a management API and dashboard. Neon's own cloud console is proprietary and the upstream neon repo ships no web UI at all, so a community control plane is the only way to run self-hosted Neon with a dashboard. EXPERIMENTAL: one container and no HA, a ~1.2 GB image, and it publishes fixed host ports for branch endpoints. Not for critical data.

configFields.help: Auto-generated, and PERMANENT — it is also the password of the internal management Postgres role, so changing it after the first launch makes the control plane unable to open its own database.

prepare.title: Create the console account and first branch
prepare.description: Registers the admin account, then creates an organization, project and `production` branch and starts its endpoint, so the install hands back a working connection string instead of an empty console.
prepare.command: set -e; API=http://127.0.0.1:3000/api; J='Content-Type: application/json'; id1() { sed -n 's/.*"id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1; }; SETUP=$(curl -fsS "$API/auth/setup" || echo ''); case "$SETUP" in *'"registration_open":true'*) ;; *) echo "pg_port=already-bootstrapped"; exit 0 ;; esac; TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$API/auth/register" -H "$J" -d "{\"name\":\"Admin\",\"email\":\"$ADMIN_EMAIL\",\"password\":\"$ADMIN_PASSWORD\"}" | sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p'); [ -n "$TOKEN" ] || { echo "pg_port=register-failed"; exit 0; }; A="Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"; ORG=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$API/organizations" -H "$J" -H "$A" -d '{"name":"Default"}' | id1); PROJ=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$API/organizations/$ORG/projects" -H "$J" -H "$A" -d '{"name":"main"}' | id1); BR=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$API/organizations/$ORG/projects/$PROJ/branches" -H "$J" -H "$A" -d '{"name":"production"}' | id1); [ -n "$BR" ] || { echo "pg_port=branch-failed"; exit 0; }; curl -fsS -X PUT "$API/organizations/$ORG/projects/$PROJ/branches/$BR/password" -H "$J" -H "$A" -d "{\"password\":\"$PG_PASSWORD\"}" >/dev/null || true; EP=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$API/organizations/$ORG/projects/$PROJ/branches/$BR/endpoint" -H "$J" -H "$A" || echo ''); PORT=$(echo "$EP" | sed -n 's/.*"port":\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1); echo "pg_port=${PORT:-unstarted}"

connection.title: Open the Neon console
connection.description: Sign in to the console to manage projects and branches. The install pre-creates the admin account plus a `production` branch with a running endpoint, so the Postgres URL below works immediately.

guide.intro: You get a Neon console for branching plus a normal Postgres connection string for the first branch.
guide.useHint: Each branch gets its own endpoint on its own port. Create a branch in the console, press Start endpoint, and copy that branch's connection string — six host ports (55432-55437) are published for endpoints, which is three concurrent branches.

outputs.label: Neon console
outputs.help: Sign in with the admin email and password below.

outputs.label: Admin email
outputs.help: The instance admin. Sign-up is closed once this account exists.

outputs.label: Database URL
outputs.help: The `production` branch endpoint. Neon assigns each endpoint its own port, so if this shows no port the endpoint has not started yet — open the console and press Start endpoint, then read the connection string there.

firstLogin.note: The admin account is created during install — use the email and password above. First boot initialises two embedded Postgres instances and can take a couple of minutes after a ~1.2 GB image pull.
